messages:
sara_cs: Heads-up — BeaconCare onboarding hit a few latency SLO bumps during large CSV imports last night. Their contract SLO is p99 <= 300ms. Observed p99 around 380-410ms during import bursts. Need quick triage + comms + a credit estimate. @kevin_sre @nina_fin @omar_legal @evan_ae

kevin_sre: Got it. Can you share the rough time windows? I'll check metrics and whether it's model decode or queueing. My hunch: bulk import saturating the batcher and causing queue waits.

sara_cs: Two windows: 23:05-23:18 and 01:02-01:08 UTC. Sample points:
```
23:08:12 POST /v1/embeddings p99 398ms host:dedicated-prod-4
- db read 95ms; model decode 240ms; batching wait 58ms
01:03:54 POST /v1/embeddings p99 382ms host:dedicated-prod-4
- cache miss; db read 105ms; model decode 230ms; queue 40ms
```

ev an_ae: FYI BeaconCare is in renewal conversation in ~8 weeks. They're on a committed monthly plan. If we owe credits we should keep it bounded and tie any ongoing remediation to a follow-up SLA check.

nina_fin: For initial sizing, if contract caps credits at monthly invoice and uses banding: propose two options
- Option A (conservative): one-off goodwill credit = 4% of monthly invoice
- Option B (conditional): 4% now, up to additional 6% (total 10%) if breach repeats within 30 days
I can run dollar amounts if you confirm their current monthly invoice.

omar_legal: Please don't word any external message as an admission of platform failure. Use "observed latency variance during onboarding imports." Confirm contract clause around "recurring" vs "isolated" incidents. Also check whether credits are automatic or require CS approval.

kevin_sre: Suggested mitigations (low-risk): 1) enable short-lived prefix KV caching for import jobs; 2) cap import concurrency to 6 parallel workers; 3) route interactive traffic to low-latency model variant. I can flip (1) and (2) in staging and run a replay tonight.

sara_cs: Proposed next steps: 1) @kevin_sre run replay with caching + concurrency cap and post numbers by 9am UTC, 2) @nina_fin produce $ amounts for Option A/B, 3) @omar_legal confirm permitted comms language, 4) I'll draft an external note to BeaconCare (include mitigations + proposed credit) for review before sending. Aim to send tomorrow morning so they see proactive handling.

nina_fin: I pulled their billing: monthly committed = $48,000. Option A = $1,920; Option B = $1,920 now, additional up to $2,880 if reoccurs within 30d. Will post a short table in thread.

omar_legal: Approved tone. Recommend: "goodwill credit in accordance with contract terms" + an explicit remediation timeline (e.g., recheck in 14 days). Avoid phrase "system outage."

ev an_ae: I'll let their procurement lead know we're investigating and will share the remediation plan + credit proposal. If they ask about capacity, offer a Dedicated capacity bump as an optional renewal add-on with clear cost delta.

kevin_sre: Test results from the replay (ran 23:05 import with caching + cap): p99 dropped from ~395ms -> ~310ms during the same load pattern. Key delta: batching wait reduced from ~58ms -> ~18ms. Will schedule the same test for 01:00 window and report by 0830 UTC.

sara_cs: Great. Please attach the 01:00 test result and I'll stitch a customer note. Nina and Omar, can you sign off on numbers + language once I post the draft?

nina_fin: Numbers look good. I'll approve the conservative Option A in the draft; leave Option B as contingency and explain the conditional cap.

omar_legal: I'll review the draft when posted. If we offer Option B, add a bullet showing the exact trigger (e.g., p99 > 300ms in any 24h sliding window twice within 30 days).

sara_cs: Draft posted (link below). Please review by 0830 UTC, aiming to send 0900. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
